cards.title: The review's 78 rows: which get fixed, in what order
cards.problem: The cloud review (read-only, on the pushed repo) found 21 defects, 41 risks and 16 cleanups; 27 rows can move a scientific number. Two carried a reproducible check and both REPRODUCE: row 9 — on any odd detector axis the sub-pixel disk refinement wraps its middle frequency to the wrong alias (the Swift wrap gives −3 where numpy and py4DSTEM's own upsampler give +2), so multicorr peak positions are off on odd crops; row 1 — the orientation bank samples one mirror triangle and the matcher has no conjugated pass, so about half of all generic zone axes land 5–22° off with no refusal (py4DSTEM's inversion pass recovers them to 0.5–1.3°); IPF colour hides it. Rows 3, 7, 33 and 35 sit beside lanes X, T and R and go to them.

cards.title: Q calibration on your cubes reads 13 % low and still says "Measured"
cards.problem: Measured this night on the app's own path: your raw 060 stride-3 cube reads a shell ratio of 1.367 (1.428 with your ellipse) against 1.155 predicted and Q 12.7 % low; your binned cube 1.374 / −12.5 %; the demo cube 1.413 / −13.45 %; Thronsen A 1.415 / −13.2 %. The (200) ring is read as (111) because your [001] majority has no {111}. What ships now: "Shell ratio unchecked" for one-shell estimates (threshold-free), and the ratio beside the Q row. A "disagrees" line needs a threshold; the pre-registered rule (a line at twice the healthy maximum only if that is under half the smallest mis-assigned) failed — and it flips on one number per side: healthy sim_Au 2.4 % measured / 4.07 % recorded; mis-assigned WS₂ 13.3 % (the (00l) l-filter case) / 18.4 % yours. So on your cube the Q row still reads "Measured". The fix — assign the ring by matching the measured ratio sequence to the crystal's shells — recovers your cube offline to +0.45 % (with ellipse) / +2.5 %, but fcc's √2 self-similarity ((200):(220) = (220):(400)) needs a bounded shell count or the zone's own ring count: a design choice, not a patch.

cards.problem: At the true Q (0.012) grain B still reads 6.50° (winner template 84) in the shipped matcher and with candidate F, at both kMax — invariant under Q, kMax and F. The bank holds B's axis [101] as its first template, so the cube is truth-bearing and the defect is on the matcher/plan side (B's in-plane angle is off-grid; the probe was flat-Ewald while the app passes a wavelength). cards.title: Ptychography after R1: the probe is right, the reconstruction is close, two things are not recorded
cards.problem: The probe now takes defocus, C12a/b and the higher-order terms and is pinned to py4DSTEM's ComplexProbe at 1.7e-6; "Use Parallax Fit" seeds defocus = −C1 — py4DSTEM's own rule (its Parallax on a probe built at +500 returns C1 = −509; the brief's +C1 was refuted before building). On the graphene cube the app's object at the same defocus correlates 0.69–0.74 raw (0.79–0.90 low-passed) with py4DSTEM's and the final errors agree within 0.1–5.6 %, but the error histories differ 8–15 % mid-run in every arm, even at defocus 0; the archived comparison could not be reproduced (both sides moved). The difference map is non-monotone in py4DSTEM too at these settings. The rule holds on the rotation branch the parallax fit used: a 180° R–Q rotation flips every coefficient and the wrong branch gives a conjugated object; the app applies no rotation guard. The probe fields are in neither the replay plan nor the sidecar nor the export provenance (lane X's file). The higher-order toggle takes the fit's terms, which py4DSTEM's own fit gets wrong on a planted case — labelled unverified.
